#### Lemma A.7 (First-order approximation error of the estimated matrices).

Let $c_{A}:=\|A\|,$ $c_{\tilde{A}}:=\|\tilde{A}\|,$ and $c_{\bar{A}}:=\|\bar{A}\|.$ Then

$$ \|\hat{A}-A\|\leq\frac{1}{2}c_{A}^{2}e^{c_{A}\Delta t}\Delta t,\qquad\|\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}\|\leq\frac{1}{2}c_{\bar{A}}(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\Delta t, $$

and

$$ \|\hat{B}-B\|\leq\frac{1}{2}(c_{A}+c_{\bar{A}})e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\|B\|\Delta t. $$

#### Proof.

For $\hat{A}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\hat{A}-A=\frac{e^{A\Delta t}-I_{d}-A\Delta t}{\Delta t}=\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}(e^{A\tau}-I_{d})A\,d\tau. $$

Taking norm in (79), and using that $\|e^{A\tau}-I_{d}\|\leq\tau c_{A}e^{c_{A}\tau},$ we obtain

$$ \|\hat{A}-A\|\leq\frac{c_{A}}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}\tau c_{A}e^{c_{A}\tau}\,d\tau\leq\frac{c_{A}^{2}}{\Delta t}e^{c_{A}\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}\tau\,d\tau=\frac{1}{2}c_{A}^{2}e^{c_{A}\Delta t}\Delta t. $$

For $\hat{\bar{A}}$ , we write

$$ \hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}=\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}\Bigl(e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}\bar{A}e^{\tilde{A}\tau}-\bar{A}\Bigr)\,d\tau. $$

Adding and subtracting $\bar{A}e^{\tilde{A}\tau}$ and taking norm, we have

$$ \displaystyle\|\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}\|\leq\frac{c_{\bar{A}}}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}\Bigl[\|e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}-I_{d}\|\,\|e^{\tilde{A}\tau}\|+\|e^{\tilde{A}\tau}-I_{d}\|\Bigr]\,d\tau. $$

Combining

$$ \|e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}-I_{d}\|\leq(\Delta t-\tau)c_{A}e^{c_{A}(\Delta t-\tau)},\qquad\|e^{\tilde{A}\tau}\|\leq e^{c_{\tilde{A}}\tau},\quad\text{and}\quad\|e^{\tilde{A}\tau}-I_{d}\|\leq\tau c_{\tilde{A}}e^{c_{\tilde{A}}\tau}, $$

with (80), we conclude that

$$ \|\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}\|\leq\frac{c_{\bar{A}}}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}\Bigl[c_{A}(\Delta t-\tau)+c_{\tilde{A}}\tau\Bigr]e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\,d\tau\leq\frac{1}{2}c_{\bar{A}}(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\Delta t. $$

Finally, for $B$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\hat{B}-B=\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}(e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}-I_{d})B\,d\tau+\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}\bar{A}M_{\tilde{A},\tau}B\,d\tau. $$

For the first term on the right-hand side of (81) we have,

$$ \displaystyle\left\|\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}(e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}-I_{d})B\,d\tau\right\|\leq\frac{\|B\|}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}(\Delta t-\tau)c_{A}e^{c_{A}(\Delta t-\tau)}\,d\tau\leq\frac{1}{2}c_{A}e^{c_{A}\Delta t}\|B\|\Delta t. $$

For the second term on the right-hand side of (81), since

$$ \|M_{\tilde{A},\tau}\|=\left\|\int_{0}^{\tau}e^{\tilde{A}(\tau-r)}\,dr\right\|\leq\int_{0}^{\tau}e^{c_{\tilde{A}}(\tau-r)}\,dr\leq\tau e^{c_{\tilde{A}}\tau}, $$

we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}\|e^{A(\Delta t-\tau)}\bar{A}M_{\tilde{A},\tau}B\|\,d\tau\leq\frac{c_{\bar{A}}\|B\|}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}e^{c_{A}(\Delta t-\tau)}\tau e^{c_{\tilde{A}}\tau}\,d\tau\leq\frac{1}{2}c_{\bar{A}}e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\|B\|\Delta t. $$

Combining both estimates (82) and (83), and using $e^{c_{A}\Delta t}\leq e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}$ , gives

$$ \|\hat{B}-B\|\leq\frac{1}{2}\left(c_{A}e^{c_{A}\Delta t}+c_{\bar{A}}e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\right)\|B\|\Delta t\leq\frac{1}{2}(c_{A}+c_{\bar{A}})e^{(c_{A}+c_{\tilde{A}})\Delta t}\|B\|\Delta t. $$

∎

#### Lemma A.8 (Assumptions on the estimated coefficients).

Assume that Assumption 5.2 holds for the original coefficients $(A,\bar{A},B)$ . Let $\hat{A}$ , $\hat{\bar{A}}$ , and $\hat{B}$ be defined by (31). Then there exists $\Delta t_{0}>0$ such that, for every $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{0}]$ , Assumption 5.2 also holds with $(A,\bar{A},B)$ replaced by $(\hat{A},\hat{\bar{A}},\hat{B})$ .

Condition (H1) is unchanged because it depends only on $Q$ , $\bar{Q}$ , and $N$ .

By (H2), there exist $\Theta_{1},\Theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}$ such that

$$ L_{1}:=A_{\beta}+B\Theta_{1},\qquad L_{2}:=\tilde{A}_{\beta}+B\Theta_{2} $$

are Hurwitz. Define

$$ \hat{L}_{1}:=\left(\hat{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)+\hat{B}\Theta_{1},\qquad\hat{L}_{2}:=\left(\hat{A}+\hat{\bar{A}}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)+\hat{B}\Theta_{2}. $$

Then

$$ \hat{L}_{1}-L_{1}=(\hat{A}-A)+(\hat{B}-B)\Theta_{1}, $$

and

$$ \hat{L}_{2}-L_{2}=(\hat{A}-A)+(\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A})+(\hat{B}-B)\Theta_{2}. $$

By Lemma A.7,

$$ \|\hat{L}_{1}-L_{1}\|+\|\hat{L}_{2}-L_{2}\|\longrightarrow 0\qquad\text{as }\Delta t\to 0. $$

Since the set of Hurwitz matrices is open, there exists $\Delta t_{0}>0$ such that $\hat{L}_{1}$ and $\hat{L}_{2}$ are Hurwitz for every $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{0}]$ . Hence the pairs $(\hat{A}_{\beta},\hat{B})$ and $(\hat{A}+\hat{\bar{A}}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d},\hat{B})$ are stabilizable. Thus Assumption 5.2 holds for the estimated coefficients. ∎

Let $\widehat{\tilde{A}}:=\hat{A}+\hat{\bar{A}}$ and consider $\hat{K},\hat{\Lambda}\in\mathbb{S}_{+}^{d}$ and $\hat{R}\in\mathbb{R}$ the solutions of the algebraic system

$$ \displaystyle\beta\hat{K} \displaystyle=Q+\hat{K}\hat{A}+\hat{A}^{\top}\hat{K}-\hat{K}\hat{B}N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K}, \displaystyle\beta\hat{\Lambda} \displaystyle=Q+\bar{Q}+\hat{\Lambda}\widehat{\tilde{A}}+\widehat{\tilde{A}}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}-\hat{\Lambda}\hat{B}N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}, \displaystyle\beta\hat{R} \displaystyle=-\frac{\lambda}{2}\left(m\log(\pi_{0}\lambda)-\log\det N\right). $$

The following proposition characterizes the optimal policy of (34) via the algebraic system (84)-(86).

#### Proposition A.9 (Auxiliary control problem).

Let $\Delta t_{0}>0$ be given by Lemma A.8, and let $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{0}]$ . Consider the auxiliary control problem

$$ \widehat{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{aux}}(\mu):=\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{add}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}r_{\lambda}^{\pi}(\hat{\mu}_{t})\,dt\,\bigg|\,\hat{\mu}_{0}=\mu\right],\qquad\mu\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}), $$

where $r_{\lambda}^{\pi}$ is defined in (3), with $r$ as in (23), and $(\hat{\mu}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ is generated by

$$ d\hat{s}_{t}=\hat{b}^{\pi}(\hat{s}_{t},\hat{\mu}_{t})\,dt,\qquad\hat{s}_{0}\sim\mu,\qquad\hat{\mu}_{t}=\Law(\hat{s}_{t}), $$

with

$$ \hat{b}^{\pi}(s,\mu):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{m}}\hat{b}(s,\mu,a)\,\pi(da\mid s,\mu), $$

and $\hat{b}$ defined in (32). Then the auxiliary control problem admits an optimal Gaussian feedback policy

$$ \hat{\pi}^{*}(\cdot\mid s,\mu)=\mathcal{N}\left(-N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}\bigl(\hat{K}(s-\bar{\mu})+\hat{\Lambda}\bar{\mu}\bigr),\frac{\lambda}{2}N^{-1}\right), $$

where $\hat{K}$ and $\hat{\Lambda}$ are the stabilizing solutions of (84) and (85), respectively. Moreover, $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{aux}}(\mu)=\hat{\mathcal{V}}^{*}(\mu)$ for every $\mu\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ . Consequently, (89) is an optimal LQR-MF-PhiBE policy.

#### Proof.

By Lemma A.8, for every $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{0}]$ , Assumption 5.2 holds with $(A,\bar{A},B)$ replaced by $(\hat{A},\hat{\bar{A}},\hat{B})$ . Moreover, by (32), the auxiliary dynamics (88) are an entropy-regularized McKean-Vlasov LQR system with drift matrices $(\hat{A},\hat{\bar{A}},\hat{B})$ and zero diffusion. Hence Proposition 5.4, applied to this auxiliary LQR problem, yields the Gaussian feedback (89) and the optimal value $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{aux}}$ .

It remains to identify the auxiliary performance with the LQR-MF-PhiBE evaluation. Let $\pi$ belong to the policy class specified in Definition 5.7, and write

$$ \widehat{\mathcal{J}}^{\pi}(\mu):=\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}r_{\lambda}^{\pi}(\hat{\mu}_{t})\,dt\,\bigg|\,\hat{\mu}_{0}=\mu\right]. $$

The auxiliary law flow has generator $\mathcal{L}_{\hat{b},0}^{\pi}$ , so $\widehat{\mathcal{J}}^{\pi}$ solves

$$ (\mathcal{L}_{\hat{b},0}^{\pi}-\beta)\widehat{\mathcal{J}}^{\pi}+r_{\lambda}^{\pi}=0. $$

If $U\in\mathcal{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{poly}}$ is another classical solution, the chain rule gives, for every $T>0$ ,

$$ U(\mu)=e^{-\beta T}U(\hat{\mu}_{T})+\int_{0}^{T}e^{-\beta t}r_{\lambda}^{\pi}(\hat{\mu}_{t})\,dt. $$

Polynomial growth and the auxiliary transversality condition imply that the boundary term converges to zero. Hence $U=\widehat{\mathcal{J}}^{\pi}$ , and therefore

$$ \hat{\mathcal{V}}^{\pi}=\widehat{\mathcal{J}}^{\pi}. $$

Taking the supremum over the common policy class in Definition 5.7 gives

$$ \hat{\mathcal{V}}^{*}=\widehat{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{aux}}. $$

Since (89) attains the auxiliary supremum, it is an optimal LQR-MF-PhiBE policy. ∎

The following lemma gives explicit bounds on the perturbation constants associated with the discounted CARE. These bounds will be used below to display the dependence on $\beta$ .

#### Lemma A.10 (Explicit bounds for the ARE perturbation constants).

Let $Q_{0}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{d}$ , $G\in\mathbb{S}_{+}^{d}$ , and $A_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ . Let $\beta\geq 0$ , set $A_{\beta}:=A_{0}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}$ , and let $X\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{d}$ be the stabilizing solution of

$$ Q_{0}+A_{\beta}^{\top}X+XA_{\beta}-XGX=0. $$

Define $\Phi_{X}:=A_{\beta}-GX,$ and $\mathcal{L}_{X}W:=\Phi_{X}^{\top}W+W\Phi_{X}.$ Let $l_{X},p_{X},q_{X}$ be the corresponding perturbation constants in the sense of [53, Theorem 3.1], namely

$$ l_{X}:=\|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}\|^{-1},\qquad p_{X}:=\left\|Z\mapsto\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}(XZ+Z^{\top}X)\right\|,\qquad q_{X}:=\left\|H\mapsto\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}(XHX)\right\|. $$

Then

$$ l_{X}\geq\frac{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}{\|X\|^{2}},\qquad p_{X}\leq\frac{2\|X\|^{3}}{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})},\qquad q_{X}\leq\frac{\|X\|^{4}}{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}. $$

Moreover,

$$ \frac{1}{\lambda_{\min}(X)}\leq\frac{\beta+2\|A_{0}\|+\|G\|\|X\|}{\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}. $$

Consequently,

$$ l_{X}\geq\frac{\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})^{2}}{\|X\|^{2}\bigl(\beta+2\|A_{0}\|+\|G\|\|X\|\bigr)}, $$

and

$$ p_{X}\leq\frac{2\|X\|^{3}\bigl(\beta+2\|A_{0}\|+\|G\|\|X\|\bigr)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})^{2}}, $$

$$ q_{X}\leq\frac{\|X\|^{4}\bigl(\beta+2\|A_{0}\|+\|G\|\|X\|\bigr)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})^{2}}. $$

#### Proof.

Since $X$ solves (90), we have

$$ A_{\beta}^{\top}X+XA_{\beta}-XGX=-Q_{0}. $$

Therefore, with $\Phi_{X}=A_{\beta}-GX$ ,

$$ \Phi_{X}^{\top}X+X\Phi_{X}=-Q_{0}-XGX\preceq-Q_{0}. $$

Let $z(t):=e^{\Phi_{X}t}z_{0}$ . From (96),

$$ \frac{d}{dt}\,z(t)^{\top}Xz(t)=z(t)^{\top}\bigl(\Phi_{X}^{\top}X+X\Phi_{X}\bigr)z(t)\leq-\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})\|z(t)\|^{2}. $$

Since $z^{\top}Xz\leq\|X\|\|z\|^{2}$ , it follows that

$$ \frac{d}{dt}\,z(t)^{\top}Xz(t)\leq-\frac{\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}{\|X\|}z(t)^{\top}Xz(t). $$

Thus

$$ z(t)^{\top}Xz(t)\leq e^{-\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})t/\|X\|}z_{0}^{\top}Xz_{0}. $$

Using $z(t)^{\top}Xz(t)\geq\lambda_{\min}(X)\|z(t)\|^{2}$ and $z_{0}^{\top}Xz_{0}\leq\|X\|\|z_{0}\|^{2}$ , we obtain

$$ \|e^{\Phi_{X}t}\|^{2}\leq\frac{\|X\|}{\lambda_{\min}(X)}e^{-\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})t/\|X\|},\qquad t\geq 0. $$

For every symmetric matrix $Y$ , the solution of $\mathcal{L}_{X}W=Y$ is

$$ W=-\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{\Phi_{X}^{\top}t}Ye^{\Phi_{X}t}\,dt. $$

Therefore, by (97),

$$ \|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}Y\|\leq\int_{0}^{\infty}\|e^{\Phi_{X}t}\|^{2}\,dt\,\|Y\|\leq\frac{\|X\|^{2}}{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}\|Y\|. $$

Hence

$$ \|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}\|\leq\frac{\|X\|^{2}}{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}, $$

which gives the first term in (91).

Next, for any $Z\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ ,

$$ \|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}(XZ+Z^{\top}X)\|\leq\|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}\|\bigl(\|XZ\|+\|Z^{\top}X\|\bigr)\leq\frac{2\|X\|^{3}}{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}\|Z\|. $$

This proves the estimate for $p_{X}$ . Similarly, for any $H\in\mathbb{S}^{d}$ ,

$$ \|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}(XHX)\|\leq\|\mathcal{L}_{X}^{-1}\|\,\|X\|^{2}\,\|H\|\leq\frac{\|X\|^{4}}{\lambda_{\min}(X)\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})}\|H\|. $$

This proves the estimate for $q_{X}$ .

It remains to prove (92). Let $v$ be a unit eigenvector of $X$ associated with $\lambda_{\min}(X)$ . Evaluating (90) on $v$ gives

$$ 0=v^{\top}Q_{0}v+2v^{\top}XA_{\beta}v-v^{\top}XGXv. $$

Since $Xv=\lambda_{\min}(X)v$ and $A_{\beta}=A_{0}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}$ , we get

$$ 0=v^{\top}Q_{0}v+2\lambda_{\min}(X)v^{\top}A_{0}v-\beta\lambda_{\min}(X)-\lambda_{\min}(X)^{2}v^{\top}Gv. $$

Hence

$$ v^{\top}Q_{0}v=\beta\lambda_{\min}(X)+\lambda_{\min}(X)^{2}v^{\top}Gv-2\lambda_{\min}(X)v^{\top}A_{0}v. $$

Using $v^{\top}Q_{0}v\geq\lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})$ , $v^{\top}Gv\leq\|G\|$ , and $-v^{\top}A_{0}v\leq\|A_{0}\|$ , we obtain

$$ \lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})\leq\bigl(\beta+2\|A_{0}\|\bigr)\lambda_{\min}(X)+\|G\|\lambda_{\min}(X)^{2}. $$

Since $\lambda_{\min}(X)\leq\|X\|$ , this implies

$$ \lambda_{\min}(Q_{0})\leq\bigl(\beta+2\|A_{0}\|+\|G\|\|X\|\bigr)\lambda_{\min}(X), $$

which proves (92). Finally, (93) follows by combining the first term in (91) with (92), and (94)-(95) follow by combining (91) with (92). ∎

#### Proof of Theorem 5.8.

We use the spectral norm. We first choose $\Delta t_{*}\in(0,1]$ sufficiently small so that the perturbation estimates below and the smallness conditions in [53, Theorem 3.1] and Lemma A.8 hold for every $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{*}]$ . Then Proposition A.9 characterizes the optimal policy $\hat{\pi}^{*}$ by (89). By Lemma A.7, choose a constant $C\geq 1$ , independent of $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{*}]$ , such that

$$ \|\hat{A}-A\|+\|\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}\|\leq\frac{C}{2}\bigl(\|A\|+\|A+\bar{A}\|\bigr)\Delta t,\qquad\|\hat{B}-B\|\leq\frac{C}{2}\|B\|\Delta t. $$

Define $C_{K}:=2\max\{1,\|K\|\}$ , $C_{\Lambda}:=2\max\{1,\|\Lambda\|\}$ , and

$$ \displaystyle C_{\tilde{A}}:=\frac{C}{2}(\|A\|+\|A+\bar{A}\|),\qquad C_{B}:=\frac{C}{2}\|B\|. $$

We also set

$$ C_{K,2}:=2C_{K}^{3}C_{\tilde{A}}+C_{K}^{4}\Bigl[2C_{B}\|N^{-1}\|\|B\|+C_{B}^{2}\|N^{-1}\|\Delta t_{*}\Bigr], $$

$$ C_{\Lambda,2}:=4C_{\Lambda}^{3}C_{\tilde{A}}+C_{\Lambda}^{4}\Bigl[2C_{B}\|N^{-1}\|\|B\|+C_{B}^{2}\|N^{-1}\|\Delta t_{*}\Bigr], $$

and

$$ C_{K,1}:=\bigl(2\|A\|+\|BN^{-1}B^{\top}\|C_{K}\bigr)C_{K,2},\qquad C_{\Lambda,1}:=\bigl(2\|A+\bar{A}\|+\|BN^{-1}B^{\top}\|C_{\Lambda}\bigr)C_{\Lambda,2}, $$

together with $C_{K,3}:=C_{B}C_{K}$ and $C_{\Lambda,3}:=C_{B}C_{\Lambda}$ . The constants above are fixed throughout the proof.

Step 1: coefficient estimates. By Lemma A.7, and by the definition of $C_{\tilde{A}}$ , we have

$$ \|\hat{A}-A\|\leq C_{\tilde{A}}\Delta t,\qquad\|\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}\|\leq C_{\tilde{A}}\Delta t,\qquad\|\hat{B}-B\|\leq C_{B}\Delta t. $$

For the proof only, set

$$ G:=BN^{-1}B^{\top},\qquad\hat{G}:=\hat{B}N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}. $$

Then

$$ \hat{G}-G=(\hat{B}-B)N^{-1}B^{\top}+BN^{-1}(\hat{B}-B)^{\top}+(\hat{B}-B)N^{-1}(\hat{B}-B)^{\top}. $$

Using (102), we obtain

$$ \|\hat{G}-G\|\leq 2C_{B}\|N^{-1}\|\|B\|\Delta t+C_{B}^{2}\|N^{-1}\|\Delta t^{2}. $$

Since $\Delta t\leq\Delta t_{*}$ , this yields

$$ \|\hat{G}-G\|\leq\Bigl[2C_{B}\|N^{-1}\|\|B\|+C_{B}^{2}\|N^{-1}\|\Delta t_{*}\Bigr]\Delta t. $$

Step 2: perturbation of the centered Riccati equation. Since $D=F=I=0$ , (25) reduces to

$$ \beta K=Q+KA+A^{\top}K-KBN^{-1}B^{\top}K. $$

Equivalently,

$$ Q+\left(A-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)^{\top}K+K\left(A-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)-KGK=0. $$

Similarly, (84) is equivalent to

$$ Q+\left(\hat{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)^{\top}\hat{K}+\hat{K}\left(\hat{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)-\hat{K}\hat{G}\hat{K}=0. $$

We now apply [53, Theorem 3.1]. This theorem compares two algebraic Riccati equations of the form

$$ Q_{0}+A_{0}^{\top}X+XA_{0}-XG_{0}X=0 $$

and

$$ (Q_{0}+\Delta Q)+(A_{0}+\Delta A)^{\top}\hat{X}+\hat{X}(A_{0}+\Delta A)-\hat{X}(G_{0}+\Delta G)\hat{X}=0. $$

For (104), we take $Q_{0}=Q$ , $A_{0}=A-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}$ , and $G_{0}=G$ . Then (105) corresponds to the coefficient differences

$$ \Delta Q_{K}:=0,\qquad\Delta A_{K}:=\hat{A}-A,\qquad\Delta G_{K}:=\hat{G}-G. $$

Let $l_{K},p_{K},q_{K}$ be the corresponding perturbation constants in [53, Theorem 3.1]. Set

$$ \varepsilon_{K}:=p_{K}\|\Delta A_{K}\|+q_{K}\|\Delta G_{K}\|,\qquad\delta_{K}:=\|\Delta A_{K}\|+\|\Delta G_{K}\|\,\|K\|,\qquad\hat{g}_{K}:=\|G+\Delta G_{K}\|. $$

By (102) and (103), we have $\varepsilon_{K}\to 0$ and $\delta_{K}\to 0$ as $\Delta t\to 0$ . Hence, after reducing $\Delta t_{*}$ if necessary, the smallness condition in [53, Theorem 3.1] holds. Moreover, the denominator in the bound of [53, Theorem 3.1] is

$$ l_{K}-2\delta_{K}+\sqrt{(l_{K}-2\delta_{K})^{2}-4l_{K}\hat{g}_{K}\varepsilon_{K}}, $$

which converges to $2l_{K}$ as $\Delta t\to 0$ . Reducing $\Delta t_{*}$ again if necessary, this denominator is bounded from below by $l_{K}$ for every $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{*}]$ . Therefore [53, Theorem 3.1] gives

$$ \|\hat{K}-K\|\leq 2\left(p_{K}\|\Delta A_{K}\|+q_{K}\|\Delta G_{K}\|\right). $$

By Lemma A.10,

$$ p_{K}\leq\frac{2\|K\|^{3}\bigl(\beta+2\|A\|+\|G\|\|K\|\bigr)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)^{2}}, $$

and

$$ q_{K}\leq\frac{\|K\|^{4}\bigl(\beta+2\|A\|+\|G\|\|K\|\bigr)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)^{2}}. $$

Since $\|K\|\leq C_{K}$ , $\|G\|=\|BN^{-1}B^{\top}\|$ , and (102)-(103) hold, (106) gives

$$ \|\hat{K}-K\|\leq\frac{2}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)^{2}}\bigl(C_{K,1}+\beta C_{K,2}\bigr)\Delta t. $$

Step 3: perturbation of the mean-field Riccati equation. Since $D=\bar{D}=F=I=0$ , (26) reduces to

$$ \beta\Lambda=Q+\bar{Q}+\Lambda\tilde{A}+\tilde{A}^{\top}\Lambda-\Lambda BN^{-1}B^{\top}\Lambda,\qquad\tilde{A}:=A+\bar{A}. $$

Equivalently,

$$ Q+\bar{Q}+\left(\tilde{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)^{\top}\Lambda+\Lambda\left(\tilde{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)-\Lambda G\Lambda=0. $$

The LQR-MF-PhiBE Riccati equation (85) is equivalent to

$$ Q+\bar{Q}+\left(\hat{A}+\hat{\bar{A}}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}+\hat{\Lambda}\left(\hat{A}+\hat{\bar{A}}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}\right)-\hat{\Lambda}\hat{G}\hat{\Lambda}=0. $$

We apply [53, Theorem 3.1] again. For (108), we take $Q_{0}=Q+\bar{Q}$ , $A_{0}=A+\bar{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}$ , and $G_{0}=G$ . Then (109) corresponds to the coefficient differences

$$ \Delta Q_{\Lambda}:=0,\qquad\Delta A_{\Lambda}:=(\hat{A}-A)+(\hat{\bar{A}}-\bar{A}),\qquad\Delta G_{\Lambda}:=\hat{G}-G. $$

By (102) and (103), we have $\|\Delta A_{\Lambda}\|\leq 2C_{\tilde{A}}\Delta t$ and

$$ \|\Delta G_{\Lambda}\|\leq\Bigl[2C_{B}\|N^{-1}\|\|B\|+C_{B}^{2}\|N^{-1}\|\Delta t_{*}\Bigr]\Delta t. $$

Let $l_{\Lambda},p_{\Lambda},q_{\Lambda}$ be the corresponding perturbation constants in [53, Theorem 3.1]. Set

$$ \varepsilon_{\Lambda}:=p_{\Lambda}\|\Delta A_{\Lambda}\|+q_{\Lambda}\|\Delta G_{\Lambda}\|,\qquad\delta_{\Lambda}:=\|\Delta A_{\Lambda}\|+\|\Delta G_{\Lambda}\|\,\|\Lambda\|,\qquad\hat{g}_{\Lambda}:=\|G+\Delta G_{\Lambda}\|. $$

The previous estimates give $\varepsilon_{\Lambda}\to 0$ and $\delta_{\Lambda}\to 0$ as $\Delta t\to 0$ . Hence, after reducing $\Delta t_{*}$ if necessary, the smallness condition in [53, Theorem 3.1] holds. Moreover, the denominator in the bound of [53, Theorem 3.1] is

$$ l_{\Lambda}-2\delta_{\Lambda}+\sqrt{(l_{\Lambda}-2\delta_{\Lambda})^{2}-4l_{\Lambda}\hat{g}_{\Lambda}\varepsilon_{\Lambda}}, $$

which converges to $2l_{\Lambda}$ as $\Delta t\to 0$ . Reducing $\Delta t_{*}$ again if necessary, this denominator is bounded from below by $l_{\Lambda}$ for every $\Delta t\in(0,\Delta t_{*}]$ . Therefore [53, Theorem 3.1] gives

$$ \|\hat{\Lambda}-\Lambda\|\leq 2\left(p_{\Lambda}\|\Delta A_{\Lambda}\|+q_{\Lambda}\|\Delta G_{\Lambda}\|\right). $$

By Lemma A.10,

$$ p_{\Lambda}\leq\frac{2\|\Lambda\|^{3}\bigl(\beta+2\|A+\bar{A}\|+\|G\|\|\Lambda\|\bigr)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q+\bar{Q})^{2}}, $$

and

$$ q_{\Lambda}\leq\frac{\|\Lambda\|^{4}\bigl(\beta+2\|A+\bar{A}\|+\|G\|\|\Lambda\|\bigr)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q+\bar{Q})^{2}}. $$

Since $\|\Lambda\|\leq C_{\Lambda}$ and $\|G\|=\|BN^{-1}B^{\top}\|$ , using (102) and (103) in (110) gives

$$ \|\hat{\Lambda}-\Lambda\|\leq\frac{2}{\lambda_{\min}(Q+\bar{Q})^{2}}\bigl(C_{\Lambda,1}+\beta C_{\Lambda,2}\bigr)\Delta t. $$

Step 4: estimate of the policy means. Define

$$ m^{*}(s,\mu):=-N^{-1}B^{\top}\bigl(K(s-\bar{\mu})+\Lambda\bar{\mu}\bigr),\qquad\hat{m}^{*}(s,\mu):=-N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}\bigl(\hat{K}(s-\bar{\mu})+\hat{\Lambda}\bar{\mu}\bigr), $$

then we have

$$ \displaystyle\hat{m}^{*}(s,\mu)-m^{*}(s,\mu) \displaystyle=N^{-1}(B^{\top}K-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K})(s-\bar{\mu})+N^{-1}(B^{\top}\Lambda-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda})\bar{\mu}. $$

For the first coefficient,

$$ B^{\top}K-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K}=B^{\top}(K-\hat{K})+(B-\hat{B})^{\top}\hat{K}. $$

Using (102) and (107),

$$ \displaystyle\|B^{\top}K-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K}\| \displaystyle\leq\|B\|\,\|\hat{K}-K\|+\|\hat{B}-B\|\,\|\hat{K}\| \displaystyle\leq 2\frac{\|B\|}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)^{2}}\bigl(C_{K,1}+\beta C_{K,2}\bigr)\Delta t+C_{B}\Delta t\bigl(\|K\|+\|\hat{K}-K\|\bigr) \displaystyle\leq\left[2\frac{\|B\|}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)^{2}}\bigl(C_{K,1}+\beta C_{K,2}\bigr)+C_{K,3}\right]\Delta t+2\frac{C_{B}}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)^{2}}\bigl(C_{K,1}+\beta C_{K,2}\bigr)\Delta t^{2}. $$

Similarly,

$$ B^{\top}\Lambda-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}=B^{\top}(\Lambda-\hat{\Lambda})+(B-\hat{B})^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}, $$

and (111) gives

$$ \displaystyle\|B^{\top}\Lambda-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}\| \displaystyle\leq\left[2\frac{\|B\|}{\lambda_{\min}(Q+\bar{Q})^{2}}\bigl(C_{\Lambda,1}+\beta C_{\Lambda,2}\bigr)+C_{\Lambda,3}\right]\Delta t+2\frac{C_{B}}{\lambda_{\min}(Q+\bar{Q})^{2}}\bigl(C_{\Lambda,1}+\beta C_{\Lambda,2}\bigr)\Delta t^{2}. $$

Substituting the last two estimates into (113) and taking norms gives exactly (35).

Step 5: cancellation of the averaged feedback for $\beta=0$ . Assume now that $\beta=0$ and $\Lambda\widetilde{A}=\widetilde{A}^{\top}\Lambda$ . Set

$$ F_{\Delta t}:=\frac{1}{\Delta t}\int_{0}^{\Delta t}e^{\widetilde{A}r}\,dr. $$

The variation-of-constants formula gives

$$ \hat{B}=F_{\Delta t}B,\qquad\widehat{\widetilde{A}}:=\hat{A}+\hat{\bar{A}}=\widetilde{A}F_{\Delta t}=F_{\Delta t}\widetilde{A}. $$

Since $F_{\Delta t}\to I_{d}$ , it is invertible for sufficiently small $\Delta t$ . The symmetry assumption and the power-series expansion of $F_{\Delta t}$ give

$$ \Lambda F_{\Delta t}=F_{\Delta t}^{\top}\Lambda. $$

Consequently

$$ P_{\Delta t}:=\Lambda F_{\Delta t}^{-1}=F_{\Delta t}^{-\top}\Lambda $$

is symmetric. Since $\Lambda\succ 0$ and $P_{\Delta t}\to\Lambda$ as $\Delta t\to 0$ , after decreasing $\Delta t_{*}$ if necessary one also has $P_{\Delta t}\succ 0$ . Moreover,

$$ P_{\Delta t}\widehat{\widetilde{A}}=\Lambda\widetilde{A},\qquad P_{\Delta t}\hat{B}=\Lambda B. $$

Substituting these identities into the exact Riccati equation for $\Lambda$ shows that

$$ Q+\bar{Q}+P_{\Delta t}\widehat{\widetilde{A}}+\widehat{\widetilde{A}}^{\top}P_{\Delta t}-P_{\Delta t}\hat{B}N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}P_{\Delta t}=0. $$

The corresponding closed-loop matrix is

$$ \widehat{\widetilde{A}}-\hat{B}N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}P_{\Delta t}=F_{\Delta t}\bigl(\widetilde{A}-BN^{-1}B^{\top}\Lambda\bigr). $$

The matrix in parentheses is Hurwitz and $F_{\Delta t}\to I_{d}$ ; hence the displayed matrix is Hurwitz for small $\Delta t$ . Thus $P_{\Delta t}$ is the symmetric stabilizing solution of the estimated Riccati equation. By uniqueness,

$$ \hat{\Lambda}=P_{\Delta t}=\Lambda F_{\Delta t}^{-1},\qquad\hat{\Lambda}\hat{B}=\Lambda B. $$

Taking transposes and using $\int(s-\bar{\mu})\,\mu(ds)=0$ proves

$$ \mathbb{E}_{s\sim\mu}\bigl[\widehat{\bar{\pi}}^{*}(s,\mu)-\bar{\pi}^{*}(s,\mu)\bigr]=0. $$

Step 6: Value function error. We now estimate the value gap between the optimal LQR policy and the LQR-MF-PhiBE policy, both evaluated in the original dynamics. Let $L:=N^{-1}B^{\top}K$ , $\hat{L}:=N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K}$ , $U:=N^{-1}B^{\top}\Lambda$ , and $\hat{U}:=N^{-1}\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}$ . By (112), the feedback means of $\pi^{*}$ and $\hat{\pi}^{*}$ are

$$ \displaystyle m^{*}(x,\nu)=-L(x-\bar{\nu})-U\bar{\nu},\qquad\hat{m}^{*}(x,\nu)=-\hat{L}(x-\bar{\nu})-\hat{U}\bar{\nu}. $$

The two Gaussian policies have covariance $\frac{\lambda}{2}N^{-1}$ . Hence, using (23) and (3), there exists a constant $c_{\lambda,N}$ , independent of $\nu$ , such that

$$ \displaystyle r_{\lambda}^{\pi^{*}}(\nu)=-\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((Q+L^{\top}NL)\operatorname{Cov}(\nu)\bigr)-\bar{\nu}^{\top}(Q+\bar{Q}+U^{\top}NU)\bar{\nu}+c_{\lambda,N}, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle r_{\lambda}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\nu)=-\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((Q+\hat{L}^{\top}N\hat{L})\operatorname{Cov}(\nu)\bigr)-\bar{\nu}^{\top}(Q+\bar{Q}+\hat{U}^{\top}N\hat{U})\bar{\nu}+c_{\lambda,N}. $$

Let $(\hat{\mu}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ be the law flow generated by the original dynamics under $\hat{\pi}^{*}$ , and set $\hat{C}_{t}:=\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mu}_{t})$ . From (114), the mean and covariance satisfy

$$ \displaystyle\dot{\bar{\hat{\mu}}}_{t}=(A+\bar{A}-B\hat{U})\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t},\qquad\dot{\hat{C}}_{t}=(A-B\hat{L})\hat{C}_{t}+\hat{C}_{t}(A-B\hat{L})^{\top}+\gamma\gamma^{\top}. $$

Moreover, by the explicit LQR value formula,

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\nu)=-\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(K\operatorname{Cov}(\nu)\bigr)-\bar{\nu}^{\top}\Lambda\bar{\nu}-R. $$

Using (118) along the flow $(\hat{\mu}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ and integrating by parts, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\mu)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}\left[-\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})+\beta\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})\right]dt. $$

Therefore, by the definition of $\mathcal{V}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\mu)-\mathcal{V}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\mu)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}\left[-\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})+\beta\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})-r_{\lambda}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})\right]dt. $$

We compute the integrand in (120). Using (117), (116), and (118), we get

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})+\beta\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})-r_{\lambda}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\hat{\mu}_{t})=\operatorname{Tr}\Bigl(\bigl[(A-B\hat{L})^{\top}K+K(A-B\hat{L})-\beta K+Q+\hat{L}^{\top}N\hat{L}\bigr]\hat{C}_{t}\Bigr) \displaystyle\qquad\qquad+\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}^{\top}\bigl[(A+\bar{A}-B\hat{U})^{\top}\Lambda+\Lambda(A+\bar{A}-B\hat{U})-\beta\Lambda+Q+\bar{Q}+\hat{U}^{\top}N\hat{U}\bigr]\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t} \displaystyle\qquad\qquad-\beta R+\gamma^{\top}K\gamma-c_{\lambda,N}. $$

The scalar term in (121) vanishes by (27). We next simplify the two matrix residuals in (121). Since (25) is equivalent to

$$ \displaystyle(A-BL)^{\top}K+K(A-BL)-\beta K+Q+L^{\top}NL=0, $$

inserting $K$ into the closed-loop equation associated with $\hat{L}$ gives

$$ \displaystyle(A-B\hat{L})^{\top}K+K(A-B\hat{L})-\beta K+Q \displaystyle+\hat{L}^{\top}N\hat{L}=(A-BL)^{\top}K+K(A-BL)-\beta K+Q+L^{\top}NL \displaystyle-(\hat{L}-L)^{\top}B^{\top}K-KB(\hat{L}-L)+\hat{L}^{\top}N\hat{L}-L^{\top}NL. $$

The first line on the right-hand side of (123) vanishes by (122). Since $L=N^{-1}B^{\top}K$ , we have $B^{\top}K=NL$ and $KB=L^{\top}N$ . Hence

$$ \displaystyle(A-B\hat{L})^{\top}K+K(A-B\hat{L})-\beta K+Q+\hat{L}^{\top}N\hat{L}=(\hat{L}-L)^{\top}N(\hat{L}-L). $$

Similarly, (26) is equivalent to

$$ \displaystyle(A+\bar{A}-BU)^{\top}\Lambda+\Lambda(A+\bar{A}-BU)-\beta\Lambda+Q+\bar{Q}+U^{\top}NU=0. $$

Inserting $\Lambda$ into the closed-loop equation associated with $\hat{U}$ and using $U=N^{-1}B^{\top}\Lambda$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle(A+\bar{A}-B\hat{U})^{\top}\Lambda+\Lambda(A+\bar{A}-B\hat{U})-\beta\Lambda+Q+\bar{Q}+\hat{U}^{\top}N\hat{U}=(\hat{U}-U)^{\top}N(\hat{U}-U). $$

Substituting (124) and (126) into (121), and then into (120), yields

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\mu)-\mathcal{V}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\mu) \displaystyle=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((\hat{L}-L)^{\top}N(\hat{L}-L)\hat{C}_{t}\bigr)dt+\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}^{\top}(\hat{U}-U)^{\top}N(\hat{U}-U)\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}\,dt. $$

In particular, $\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\mu)-\mathcal{V}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\mu)\geq 0.$ It remains to estimate the right-hand side of (127). From Step 4, we have already proved

$$ \displaystyle\|B^{\top}K-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K}\|\leq C\Delta t,\qquad\|B^{\top}\Lambda-\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}\|\leq C\Delta t. $$

Therefore, by the definitions of $L,\hat{L},U,\hat{U}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\|\hat{L}-L\|+\|\hat{U}-U\| \displaystyle\leq\|N^{-1}\|\left(\|\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{K}-B^{\top}K\|+\|\hat{B}^{\top}\hat{\Lambda}-B^{\top}\Lambda\|\right)\leq C\Delta t. $$

Because $K$ and $\Lambda$ are the stabilizing solutions of the discounted CAREs, the shifted matrices

$$ A_{\beta}-BL,\qquad\widetilde{A}_{\beta}-BU,\qquad A_{\beta}:=A-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d},\quad\widetilde{A}_{\beta}:=A+\bar{A}-\frac{\beta}{2}I_{d}, $$

are Hurwitz. Since $\hat{L}\to L$ and $\hat{U}\to U$ , after decreasing $\Delta t_{*}$ there exist $C,c>0$ , independent of $\Delta t$ , such that

$$ \|e^{(A_{\beta}-B\hat{L})t}\|+\|e^{(\widetilde{A}_{\beta}-B\hat{U})t}\|\leq Ce^{-ct},\qquad t\geq 0. $$

The mean equation in (117) therefore gives

$$ e^{-\beta t}|\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}|^{2}=\left|e^{(\widetilde{A}_{\beta}-B\hat{U})t}\bar{\mu}\right|^{2}\leq Ce^{-2ct}|\bar{\mu}|^{2}. $$

For the covariance, variation of constants yields

$$ \hat{C}_{t}=e^{(A-B\hat{L})t}\operatorname{Cov}(\mu)e^{(A-B\hat{L})^{\top}t}+\int_{0}^{t}e^{(A-B\hat{L})u}\gamma\gamma^{\top}e^{(A-B\hat{L})^{\top}u}\,du. $$

Consequently,

$$ e^{-\beta t}\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{C}_{t})\leq Ce^{-2ct}\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Cov}(\mu))+C|\gamma|^{2}\int_{0}^{t}e^{-\beta(t-u)}e^{-2cu}\,du. $$

Since $\beta>0$ , integration in time and Fubini’s theorem give

$$ \int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}\left(\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{C}_{t})+|\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}|^{2}\right)dt\leq C\bigl(1+m_{2}(\mu)\bigr), $$

with $C$ independent of $\Delta t$ . The same pointwise estimates imply

$$ e^{-\beta t}\left(\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{C}_{t})+|\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}|^{2}\right)\longrightarrow 0,\qquad t\to\infty, $$

and hence justify the boundary limit used in (119). Combining (127), (129), and (130), we get

$$ \displaystyle 0\leq\mathcal{V}^{\pi^{*}}(\mu)-\mathcal{V}^{\hat{\pi}^{*}}(\mu) \displaystyle\leq C\left(\|\hat{L}-L\|^{2}+\|\hat{U}-U\|^{2}\right)\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t}\left(\operatorname{Tr}(\hat{C}_{t})+|\bar{\hat{\mu}}_{t}|^{2}\right)dt\leq C\Delta t^{2}\bigl(1+m_{2}(\mu)\bigr). $$

This proves (36). ∎

#### Lemma A.11 (Second-moment bound for the MKV-LQR flow when $\beta=0$ ).

Assume Assumption 5.2 with $\beta=0$ . Let $(K,\Lambda)$ be the stabilizing solution of (25)-(26), and let $\pi^{*}$ be the Gaussian feedback in (29). Let $(s_{t},\mu_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ be the MKV dynamics (5) under $\pi^{*}$ , with $\Law(s_{t})=\mu_{t}$ and $\mu_{0}\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ . Then there exist constants $C\geq 1$ and $\kappa>0$ such that, for every $t\geq 0$ ,

$$ m_{2}(\mu_{t})\leq Ce^{-2\kappa t}m_{2}(\mu_{0})+C|\gamma|^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

Let $\bar{\mu}_{t}:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}x\,\mu_{t}(dx)$ and set $\xi_{t}:=s_{t}-\bar{\mu}_{t}$ . Under (29), $\int_{\mathbb{R}^{m}}a\pi^{*}(da\mid x,\mu)=-N^{-1}B^{\top}\bigl(K(x-\bar{\mu})+\Lambda\bar{\mu}\bigr).$ Since $\sigma(x,\mu,a)=\gamma$ , the closed-loop MKV dynamics is

$$ ds_{t}=\bigl[A_{K}(s_{t}-\bar{\mu}_{t})+A_{\Lambda}\bar{\mu}_{t}\bigr]dt+\gamma\,dW_{t}, $$

where $A_{K}:=A-BN^{-1}B^{\top}K$ and $A_{\Lambda}:=A+\bar{A}-BN^{-1}B^{\top}\Lambda.$ Taking expectation gives $\dot{\bar{\mu}}_{t}=A_{\Lambda}\bar{\mu}_{t}$ . Since $\Lambda$ is the stabilizing solution of (26), $A_{\Lambda}$ is Hurwitz. Hence there exist $C_{\Lambda}\geq 1$ and $\kappa_{\Lambda}>0$ such that

$$ |\bar{\mu}_{t}|^{2}\leq C_{\Lambda}e^{-2\kappa_{\Lambda}t}|\bar{\mu}_{0}|^{2}. $$

The estimate for $\xi_{t}$ follows from the same quadratic energy argument used in [12, Lemma A.8]. Indeed, $\xi_{t}$ solves

$$ d\xi_{t}=A_{K}\xi_{t}\,dt+\gamma\,dW_{t}, $$

and the stabilizing property of $K$ gives a Lyapunov function for $A_{K}$ . Applying Itô’s formula to this quadratic Lyapunov function and using Gronwall’s inequality yields constants $C_{K}\geq 1$ and $\kappa_{K}>0$ such that

$$ \mathbb{E}|\xi_{t}|^{2}\leq C_{K}e^{-2\kappa_{K}t}\mathbb{E}|\xi_{0}|^{2}+C_{K}|\gamma|^{2}. $$

Finally, since $m_{2}(\mu_{t})=\mathbb{E}|s_{t}|^{2}=\mathbb{E}|\xi_{t}|^{2}+|\bar{\mu}_{t}|^{2}$ and $m_{2}(\mu_{0})=\mathbb{E}|\xi_{0}|^{2}+|\bar{\mu}_{0}|^{2},$ taking $\kappa:=\min\{\kappa_{K},\kappa_{\Lambda}\}$ and increasing $C$ if necessary gives

$$ m_{2}(\mu_{t})\leq Ce^{-2\kappa t}m_{2}(\mu_{0})+C|\gamma|^{2}. $$

∎
